messages:
sarah: Heads-up — our nightly backup/rotation job hit a burst of GCP KMS ResourceExhausted errors around 02:14 UTC. ~30% of decrypts returned 429 and we saw token-level latency spikes. Autos-retries recovered most ops but we had a short window of degraded throughput. Opening thread to review retry strategy, DEK cache hardening, and audit signals.

ajay: Can you paste a couple of log snippets?

sarah: Sure — trimmed logs below showing the failure mode we saw:
```
2026-03-19T02:14:12Z ERROR crypto: decrypt failed: google.api_core.exceptions.ResourceExhausted: 429 Resource exhausted.
stack: google.cloud.kms_v1.services.key_management_service.client -> projects/.../locations/us-central1/keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/...
2026-03-19T02:14:13Z WARN runtime: retrying decrypt (attempt 2) after backoff 200ms
2026-03-19T02:14:14Z ERROR crypto: decrypt failed: google.api_core.exceptions.ResourceExhausted
```

liz: Did our alerts trigger? I didn't see a paging incident.

ops-bot: metric alert (kms.decrypt_error_rate) fired for 2m at 02:15 UTC; severity: low.

sarah: Alert fired but severity low because error rate was short-lived. Concern is this pattern could surface during large customer key rotations or bulk restores. Also want to confirm failed decrypts are captured in audit logs and flagged for compliance.

ajay: Possible causes: GCP KMS regional per-project QPS limits, or a transient quota from other workloads in the project. We currently do linear backoff with fixed retry attempts=4, base=200ms, no jitter.

liz: From security perspective: we need two things — (1) ensure audit logs include every DEK decrypt failure with requester identity, and (2) make sure RBAC grants limit blast radius. Which service account is this job using?

sarah: Job runs under svc-rotation@redwood-prod. It has roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter scoped to the key ring. Not using any broad editor roles.

kevin: Actionable proposal:
- Switch to exponential backoff with full jitter (base=100ms, cap=5s), max attempts=6.
- Add per-key circuit breaker: trip after X errors in 30s, then fallback to cached DEK if available.
- Temporarily increase local DEK cache TTL from 5m -> 20m during rotation windows.
- Emit a distinct metric for KMS 429s and add an alert escalation policy if sustained >1m.

ajay: +1. Also recommend adding a slow-path where, if decrypts fail for a given customer-encryption-key, we pause rotation for that key and enqueue for manual retry to avoid hammering KMS.

liz: For audit/compliance: ensure failed decrypts are forwarded to Sumo with fields: requester_sa, key_id, operation_id, error_code. I'll open a permissions review to confirm no other SA can call these keys.

sarah: I've created a short repro job to replay high concurrency decrypts in us-central1 to validate behavior. Will run it in staging first.

ajay: For the retry code, I'll change the client wrapper to: exponential backoff + full jitter, attempt cap=6, and add a permissive circuit-breaker per-key with cooldown 60s. I'll push a draft PR and tag for review.

kevin: Runbook update: add a step "if KMS 429s observed during rotation: reduce concurrency -> enable DEK cache TTL bump -> contact cloud provider support if >10m sustained". I'll draft.

liz: Also add a query to the compliance dashboard that shows decrypt failures by key and SA for the last 24h. We need that for audits.

sarah: After the test, I'll post results here. Preliminary staging replay produced the same 429s at 6k qps but our backoff + jitter reduced failed ops to <2%.

deploy-bot: CI build passed for ajay/kms-backoff-pr (#4127).

ajay: PR linked in thread: https://git.redwood.internal/p/4127 — includes unit tests and an integration test that simulates ResourceExhausted.

liz: I'll do a quick RBAC sweep and post any privilege anomalies by EOD.

kevin: Opening ticket INC-2026 to track follow-ups and runbook changes.

sarah: Thanks all. Next steps: ajay -> merge backoff PR and run staging canary; liz -> RBAC + audit log queries; kevin -> runbook + alert rule changes. Will reconvene if staging shows issues. :thumbsup:
